issues.legal_issue: A firm and its other partners are not bound by a partner’s sub-lease when the transaction was not made in the firm’s name or in a manner expressing or implying an intention to bind the firm.
material_facts: The appellant granted the sub-lease to one partner alone, and it was not executed in the name of the partnership firm.
The courts below found that the partner obtained the sub-lease alone and did not act on behalf of the firm.
The appellant’s case in the courts below was that the partner was a benamidar for the firm; the firm’s liability based on the transaction as a partnership transaction was not established.
issues.conclusion: The decree was properly limited to respondents 4 and 5; the firm and the other partners were not liable under the sub-lease.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 requires an act or instrument by a partner to be done or executed in the firm’s name, or in another manner expressing or implying an intention to bind the firm. The Court distinguished Karmali Abdulla Allarakia v. Vora Karimji Jiwanji and Gouthwaite v. Duckworth, where the underlying transaction was a partnership transaction; Mathura Nath Choudhury v. Sreejukta Bageswari Rani, concerning a borrowing connected with partnership business; Pandiri Veeranna v. Grandi Veerabhadraswami, concerning authority inferable from surrounding circumstances; Lakshmishankar Devshankar v. Motiram Vishnuram, concerning money applied to firm debts or legitimate firm purposes; and Gordhandas Chhotalal Seth v. Mahant Shri Raghubirdasji Gangaramji, concerning a managing partner’s debt for partnership business. Those decisions did not assist because the sub-lease here was not found to be a partnership transaction.

rule.if: partnership_transaction_liability_claim and sublease_not_made_in_firm_name and not intention_to_bind_firm

predicates.partnership_transaction_liability_claim: A claimant seeks to hold a firm and its other partners liable for a transaction made by one partner.
predicates.sublease_not_made_in_firm_name: The sub-lease was made with an individual partner and was not executed in the firm’s name.
predicates.intention_to_bind_firm: The transaction was made in a manner expressing or implying an intention to bind the firm.
predicates.firm_and_other_partners_not_bound_by_sub: The firm and its other partners are not liable under the sub-lease.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks to impose liability on a firm and its other partners for an individual partner’s sub-lease, and the sub-lease was not made in the firm’s name and did not show an intention to bind the firm, the firm and the other partners are not bound by it.

issues.legal_issue: An appellant may not replace the case presented in the courts below with a materially different factual theory on appeal.
material_facts: The appellant’s case in the courts below was that the partner took the sub-lease as a benamidar for the partnership firm.
In the Supreme Court, the appellant relied on the firm’s possession of the colliery to argue that the partnership had already existed when the sub-lease was obtained, a case not previously advanced.
issues.conclusion: The Court would not permit the appellant to make out the new case on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that it would not be proper to permit an appellant to advance an entirely new case at the appellate stage when the opposing parties had been required to meet a different case in the courts below.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal.
predicates.new_factual_theory_not_advanced_below: The appellant relies on a materially different factual theory from the one presented in the courts below.
predicates.appellate_court_does_not_allow_new_case: The appellate court does not permit the appellant to make out the new case.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, when the appellant advances a materially different factual theory from the one presented in the courts below, the appellate court does not permit the appellant to make out that new case.
